_readme: This file is the signature -> repo/verb map for scripts/triage.py, the act-loop that
replaced per-message LLM triage in #alerts. A 'signature' is `source:external_id`
from ~/.hermes/watchdog.db's `events` table (source = one of slack_alert, uk,
docker_homelab, docker_vps, hermes_log, op_refs_homelab, op_refs_vps).
MATCH TARGETS (this is the part that was missing in the first draft of this file):
`rules`/`ignore` are matched against TWO candidate strings per event, in order, first
match wins across BOTH: `source:external_id` (the raw form) and
`source:normalize_title(title)` (the human-readable form, same normalize_title() as
scripts/watchdog-poll.py). For a grouped source (slack_alert, hermes_log) these are
usually the SAME string, since that source's external_id already IS
normalize_title(title) — see aggregate_slack_batch()/poll_hermes_logs(). For a state
source (uk, docker_homelab, docker_vps, op_refs_*) they differ: uk's external_id is an
opaque, unglobbable UptimeKuma monitor id ('204'), so `uk:macmini-dev-host-push` (the
title-derived target) is what makes that source mappable at all — a rule written
against the numeric id would break the moment the monitor is recreated.
Matching is glob-style (Python fnmatch: `*`, `?`, `[seq]`). `rules` matched
top-to-bottom, first match wins. `ignore` is checked FIRST, before everything else — a
match sends the item straight to state `ignored`: never carded, never escalated, never
even in the digest. Use `ignore` ONLY for a genuine recovery or a known-benign pattern
you have looked at and decided is truly nothing — see `ignoreUnstructuredSlackProse`
below for the very different case of 'this looks like it might matter but isn't
structured enough to auto-route'. No rule match at all -> the item stays unmapped
(state `new`, never escalates, carried silently) and its signature shows up in the
once-a-day digest so this file can grow deliberately instead of silently missing real
problems.
`ignoreUnstructuredSlackProse` (bool) is a STRUCTURAL filter, not a glob list, checked
AFTER `ignore`: any `slack_alert` item whose title does not start with a recognized
bot-alert shape (`[`, the siren emoji, checkmark, warning, or a bold-mrkdwn warning) is
routed to STATE_NOTE — NOT `ignored`. This distinction is load-bearing: `ignored` is
terminal AND invisible, and this DB genuinely contains rows like a human-written 'the
1Password rate-limit root cause is X, the two-line fix is Y' diagnosis that was never
shipped — dropping that into `ignored` would recreate the exact failure this whole
redesign exists to kill. STATE_NOTE is ALSO terminal (never escalates, never gets its
own card) but IS surfaced, once a day, under its own heading in the digest, so a real
diagnosis stays visible instead of vanishing. WHY THE FILTER EXISTS AT ALL: before
#alerts was silenced (see config.yaml), Hermes replied in that channel to every
message, and watchdog-poll.py's slack_alert poller ingested those replies right
alongside real bot alerts — hundreds of German/English sentences ('Alles grün.
„:ok_hand:“') sitting in `events` as if they were alert signatures. Silencing the
channel stops NEW ones; this flag is what keeps the existing backlog visible-but-quiet
instead of either flooding the channel with cards or disappearing into `ignored`.
`verb` is the other rule outcome, instead of `repo`: routes to a declared, code-side
ALLOWLISTED local command (VERB_ALLOWLIST in scripts/triage.py) rather than a sideclaw
episode — this file names a KEY ('env-check'), never a command; the argv is decided in
code, on purpose, so a policy edit alone can never run something arbitrary. Terminal
state for a verb outcome is `needs_human`, with the command's own output inlined on
the card. Used for op_refs_homelab/op_refs_vps: a dead 1Password ref is a deterministic,
already-diagnosed condition (hermes-ops.sh's env-check already returns the dangling
item name) — dispatching an episode to 're-discover' it would be slower AND worse: a
bare item name in a dispatched verdict can collide with sideclaw's own
`op://vault/item/field` secret-scan pattern and get withheld, whereas env-check's output
reaching the card directly does not.
Every `repo` value MUST resolve under `root` in config/dispatch-repos.json and MUST
NOT appear in that file's `deny` list — scripts/triage.py checks the deny list
itself before ever shelling out, so a rule naming a denied repo just silently never
escalates (logged to stderr) rather than crashing, but it is still a bug in this
file, not a feature. `homelab-private` is denied and 'shelfmark' below is why it is
in `ignore` rather than mapped to it: shelfmark is a third-party image
(ghcr.io/calibrain/shelfmark) running in the private compose file — nothing to
dispatch an investigation against even if the repo were reachable.
THE CONVENTION FOR WHICH REPO OWNS AN INFRA-SIGNAL ALERT (this is the part a real VPS
outage trace caught wrong once already — the argo rules below used to point at `argo`):
an infra-signal alert about a RollHook-managed app maps to the repo that owns its
COMPOSE FILE AND DEPLOY TARGET, not the repo that owns its source. `argo` is
compose-managed manually inside `vps` (`apps/argo/compose.yml`, `make argo-up` —
nothing in argo's own repo redeploys it), so a downed argo container maps to `vps`.
Most OTHER vps-hosted apps in this policy (audio-gateway, weatherorb,
image-gen, image-share) are the opposite: dispatch-repos.json's own comment documents
that they deploy to the VPS on every push to THEIR OWN repo's master (GitHub Actions ->
RollHook), so a code fix in their own repo auto-redeploys — mapping those to their own
repo is correct and deliberate, not an oversight to 'fix' the same way. Before adding a
new vps-app rule, check `vps/apps/<name>/compose.yml` AND whether that app's own repo
has its own deploy workflow before deciding which direction the rule should point. The
HyperDX-origin alerts (job.reaped, podcast.failed, vps-edge-*, ...) map to `vps` for a
related but distinct reason: their threshold/definition lives in
vps/observability/alerts/*.json, which is where THAT fix lands regardless of which
service the alert is about.
To extend: run
sqlite3 ~/.hermes/watchdog.db "SELECT source, external_id, title FROM events
WHERE resolved_at IS NULL ORDER BY first_seen DESC LIMIT 40;"
and add a rule (or an ignore pattern) for anything real that shows up unmapped —
remembering a `uk` rule almost always wants the title-derived target, e.g.
`uk:some-monitor-name-push`, never the bare numeric id.
`evidence` (list, optional on any `repo` rule) fences DECLARED runtime-state probes into
the escalation brief — the fix for every real episode so far (weatherorb, vps, hermes-agent)
coming back `nextAction: human` citing the SAME reason: the dispatched episode runs in a
read-only repo WORKTREE, which has the repo but never the live machine. Same closed-set
principle as `verb`: this file names KEYS from EVIDENCE_ALLOWLIST in scripts/triage.py,
never a command. Seeded: `weatherorb-health` (weatherorb's own var/health.json, summarized),
`gateway-starts`/`hermes-log-tail` (Hermes's own gateway restart ledger + its error log
sliced at the current process start, per skills/hermes-gateway/SKILL.md Rule 0),
`kuma-push-last` (the live UptimeKuma push-heartbeat text for a `uk`-sourced cluster
member — this is NOT in `events.payload_json`, which is only `{type, status}`; it exists
only in the raw #alerts Slack text, which watchdog-poll.py's `skip_uk_push` deliberately
drops before it ever reaches `events`). An unknown evidence key drops the WHOLE rule at
load, loudly, same as an unknown verb.
`quietResolveHours` (default 2, see DEFAULT_QUIET_RESOLVE_HOURS's own comment) closes a
GROUPED item (slack_alert, hermes_log) whose signal has produced no new occurrence in
that many hours — those two sources otherwise never disappearance-resolve at all
(watchdog-poll.py's sweep_stale_grouped only clears them after 7 idle DAYS, deliberate
housekeeping, not signal). A `✅ <same alert text>` HyperDX recovery message resolves a
slack_alert item immediately instead, on the next run, whenever one is found — strictly
better than waiting out the timer. NEITHER path ever means "fixed": the resolved card
always says "signal quiet since <time>" or "recovery message observed: …", never that.
`repos` (object, keyed by repo name) is the DIFFERENT half of this file: it does not
route a signature, it governs what scripts/lifecycle/merge.py's `merge`/`deploy`/`liveness`
machinery is allowed to do once a triage-opened `implement` episode has a confirmed,
validated pull request. Per-repo entry:
autoMergePaths  glob list — PRIMARY merge gate. EVERY changed path in the diff must
match one, or `merge` refuses outright; a repo absent from `repos` or
with no autoMergePaths refuses too — there is no implicit allow.
noCiRequired    bool — an explicit acknowledgement that this repo has zero PR-time
required checks, so `merge` treats that as a KNOWN condition rather
than silently reading `mergeable_state: clean` as "CI passed" (it is
vacuously clean with nothing having run). Omit/false + zero check-runs
on the head commit = refused, on purpose — that inversion is the point.
deploy          a KEY from scripts/clients/rollout.py's own closed DEPLOY allowlist (ROLLOUTS),
never a command — same closed-set principle as `verb`/`evidence` above.
autoDeploy      bool, default false. Ships OFF everywhere: the mechanism lands reviewed
but inert. Flip it per-repo only after watching a run of merges land
cleanly with autoDeploy still off. See docs/triage.md for how.
liveness        a KEY from triage.py's own LIVENESS_ALLOWLIST (same closed-set shape),
run after a deploy to positively confirm the intended state before the
item resolves — an alert going quiet is also what a fully-down service
looks like, so silence alone is never proof of a fix here either.
deployOnMerge   bool, default false. Declares this repo's CI/CD as merge-IS-deploy
(GitHub Actions -> RollHook, DESIGN.md § Deploy, STATE.md §47/§48
item 1b) — a successful merge itself IS the deploy, with the Actions
run id as its receipt (there is no ssh path here to ask, unlike
`deploy`/`autoDeploy` above). poll_validation_jobs() checks
`deploy.attempted`/`.ok` FIRST, so this key only takes effect once that
ssh-deploy branch has already said no — the two are naturally mutually
exclusive without an explicit guard, since a deployOnMerge repo
deliberately never declares `autoDeploy` too. A merge in a
deployOnMerge repo goes straight to `liveness_pending` on the merge
commit sha, never to `merged`, UNLESS the merge result carried no
usable 40-char-hex mergeCommit — that falls through to `merged` with a
reason, on purpose (a probe with nothing to compare against would just
sit until liveness_deadline and reopen, worse than an honest `merged`).
`vps` is seeded below at the narrowest possible scope (`observability/**` only) — its
own compose files, apps and everything else stay outside every one of these gates.
`argo` is seeded with `deployOnMerge` + `liveness: argo-commit-live` and ONE canary path
in `autoMergePaths` (`docs/DEPLOY-VERIFICATION.md`, a file nothing in argo reads or builds): the
owner-authorized scope for the Wave 5 stop-condition exercise (dotfiles
docs/waves/PLAN.md header, 2026-09-10). Every other path in argo stays outside the
gate — merge_gate_check() in scripts/lifecycle/merge.py refuses it OUTOFSCOPE. Widening
past the canary is a separate operator decision — do not add paths here to "complete"
this entry.
`hostVerbs` (list) is the FIFTH closed allowlist's own rule set — the owner's 2026-09-11
decision that warden may run an idempotent host-level restart itself, rather than card
`needs_human` for a fix it is already confident in (STATE.md, docs/history/state-log.md §59). Same
match-target/first-match-wins shape as `rules` above: each entry is
`{"match": "<glob>", "verb": "<key>"}`, and `verb` names a KEY from
HOST_VERB_ALLOWLIST in scripts/triage.py, never an argv — an unknown key drops the whole
rule at load, loudly, same as `rules`'/`evidence`'s own unknown-key handling.
maybe_auto_remediate() ALSO requires the item's own folded investigate verdict to RANK AT
OR ABOVE `hostVerbMinConfidence` (default "medium" — validated at load to one of
high/medium/low, anything else falls back to "medium" with a stderr line) before it will
ever run one of these — a `hostVerbs` match alone is not enough. `high` is deliberately NOT
the floor here (unlike auto-implement's own confidence gate): a restart from
HOST_VERB_ALLOWLIST is idempotent, confirmed by a POSITIVE liveness probe before the item is
ever marked done, and capped at `hostVerbMaxAttempts` — so a wrong guess costs one restart
and a `needs_human` card carrying the receipt, which is cheaper than a human running that
exact same restart by hand. `hostVerbCooldownHours` (default 6) and `hostVerbMaxAttempts`
(default 2) bound repeats against the SAME item, mirroring `cooldownHours` above but against
the `operations` ledger instead of `dispatches`. Seeded with the three signatures behind the
recurring hermes-agent gateway restart (uk:175 `Hermes Agent`, uk:185 `Hermes Watchdog -
Push`, and the hermes_log `session-is-closed` reconnect signal) mapped to
`restart-hermes-gateway`. uk:193 (`Research Gateway - HTTP`) was never seeded and is now
moot: the VPS research-gateway instance is retired (2026-09-26), the mini instance is the
only one, and its Kuma monitors are being removed.
`proposeMappingsAgeDays` (default 7) gates scripts/triage.py's propose_mappings() —
the ONE LLM call anywhere in that file, and the only mechanism that ever grows THIS
file automatically. Once every 24h it batches every signature that has sat unmapped
(no `rules` match) in state `new` for at least this many days — a fresh signature may
still be a one-off, and mapping it this early wastes a whole investigate episode — and
asks the SAME deepseek-v4.1-flash brain config.yaml already configures to propose `map`
(append a rule — a wrong one costs one wasted read-only episode), `ignore` (append to
the ignore list), or `unsure` (leave unmapped, not re-asked for 7 more days). Every
applied entry below is stamped `proposedAt`/`proposedBy: "triage-auto"` plus the
model's own one-line reason, then committed (never pushed) by that same script — read
docs/triage.md's PROPOSE MAPPINGS section before touching an auto-added entry.

argo._note: autoMergePaths is the CANARY SCOPE ONLY — one file nothing in argo reads or builds, owner-authorized for the Wave 5 stop-condition exercise (2026-09-10, STATE.md §54). merge_gate_check() in scripts/lifecycle/merge.py refuses every other path OUTOFSCOPE. Widening this list is a separate operator decision; do not add paths here to 'complete' this entry.

hermes-agent._note: No autoMergePaths — hermes-agent stays NOT auto-mergeable (FLOWS.md flow 5). `liveness` is here only so a host-verb restart (maybe_auto_remediate(), STATE_LIVENESS_PENDING) has a repo-scoped key to read; it is never reached via the merge/deploy chain because this repo never gets that far.

homelab._note: §93 — the Kuma monitor definitions are the one auto-merge scope: a monitor fix lands, `uk-sync` applies it on the homelab server, and the item's own monitor must report UP afterwards (kuma-push-fresh). sync.py, the Makefile and compose files stay outside — warden must not write the code it runs. homelab has no PR-time CI; the gate is the independent step-7 review, which blocks a change that loosens detection without evidence (VALIDATION_GATE_QUESTIONS).

weatherorb._note: §105 — fully unattended (landed 2026-09-28 by Hermes on the owner's standing directive that every PR be auto-reviewed, merged, deployed and verified — no separate owner decision was quoted for weatherorb: it is private and only he files its issues, the narrow watchdog/tests/docs scope of §93 was friction). `**` is exactly the default unattended scope a repo with no entry gets (merge.py DEFAULT_REPO_ENTRY): every path NEVER_AUTO_MERGE does not name. Declared here rather than by omission so this file says it and a later change to the default cannot silently narrow this repo. `weatherorb-pull` fast-forwards the live checkout AND kickstarts tileserver/sync, so a merge is the rollout for the periodic jobs and the long-running ones alike; the WeatherOrb Watchdog push monitor reporting UP plus its synthetic trip (§103) is the proof for a uk-origin item, an issue-origin item lands `merged` with no monitor of its own. Since §107 (owner, 2026-09-29) no path class stops here: Makefile, ops/*.plist (reloaded by `make launchd-install` inside weatherorb-pull), .github/workflows (deploy-edge runs on the merge), Dockerfiles, package.json, bun.lock/uv.lock and pyproject.toml merge like any other file. No PR-time CI; the step-7 review is the gate.

research-gateway._note: §93 — merge IS deploy: the mini's CI-gated, idle-gated poller (scripts/mini-deploy.sh) rolls master out, and mini-checkout-live confirms the poller's checkout carries the merge commit and /health answers ok. CI runs on push to master only (no PR checks), so noCiRequired here means the implement tier's own pre-push checks plus the step-7 review gate the merge, and CI still gates the deploy: a red master never reaches the checkout, liveness times out, the item reopens with the PR in its history. scripts/**, Makefile, launchd/**, package.json and bun.lock stay outside — deploy definitions and dependencies are never auto-merged.

rules._note: §100 — the self-audit's findings are warden's own defects: investigated and implemented like any alert, merged only by the owner's Argo click (merge_approval).
